  • Industry observers note that so far major updates have brought the likes of buffs, balance adjustments, art updates, UI improvements, bug fixes, and more - and MegaCrit has also made other substantial adjustments including the jettisoning of third act boss Doormaker, after it decided the encounter was overly complex.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that slay the Spire 2, which released into early access earlier this year, is expanding once more with a major fresh beta patch. This introduces the deckbuilder's first new character since launch - a whimsical musician armed with a bow - alongside two new modes, and more.

It has been revealed that when Slay the Spire 2 arrived back in March, it was to much enthusiastic acclaim. Eurogamer's Bertie Purchie is a big fan, and has trumpeted its successes on multiple occasions, calling the sequel's co-op mode "transformative". And it was a commercial hit too, managing to shift over 5m copies in just a month of release. All of which means there are plenty of eyes on Slay the Spire 2, eager to see what developer MegaCrit does next.

Industry observers note that so far major updates have brought the likes of buffs, balance adjustments, art updates, UI improvements, bug fixes, and more - and MegaCrit has also made other substantial adjustments including the jettisoning of third act boss Doormaker, after it decided the encounter was overly complex. And now, as 2026 nears its conclusion, the studio has released its "biggest (beta) patch yet", including a sweep of major additions.

Sources indicate that as per MegaCrit's v0.113.0 patch notes, the headliner is The Fool; Slay the Spire 2's first fresh character, who's described as a "silly musician who wields a bow". Unsurprisingly, The Fool doesn't arrive in their final form, and the studio notes it expects to make a "great number of content and balance changes" before the character is ready for the main branch.

Accompanying The Fool are two upcoming game modes: Blitz and Dread. Blitz is described as a "condensed and chaotic" mode focused on deckbuilding. Unlocked after completing an Ascension run of any difficulty, it comes with five levels of Ascension shared across all characters. "The Merchant's wares feel a bit off," MegaCrit teases, "the map is gone, and Gold no longer matters??".

Industry observers note that if you're looking for a more gruelling challenge, though, there's the "brutally difficult" new Dread mode, designed for players who've reached Ascension 10 on all characters, including The Fool. All ascension modifiers are enabled, according to MegaCrit, while bosses are stronger and buff all enemies found across their Act. And if that's still not enough to get your heart racing, MegaCrit notes curses will also pile up as you climb the Spire.

Beyond the headline stuff, v0.113.0 tweaks rest sites so they appear one floor earlier every act, and that's alongside the usual list of UI changes, art additions, nerfs, balance adjustments, and more. Full patch notes can be found on Steam.

According to recent reports, those players eager to put Slay the Spire 2's latest additions through their paces will need to enable the beta branch by right-clicking on Slay the Spire 2 in their Steam library and navigating to Properties > Game Versions & Betas and selecting 'public-beta' from the dropdown menu. MegaCrit notes the game's main branch has also been updated with all content and changes from the previous beta.

  • "My plan was never to be CEO for life," Wester said.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, paradox Interactive, publishers of umpteen strategy genre stalwarts including Crusader Kings, Europa Universalis, and Hearts of Iron, have unveiled prepares to switch overlords early next year. Fredrik Wester will make way for Mattias Lilja, as the deputy CEO takes the throne.

While the move's been unveiled this week, Lilja will properly become boss from January 4th, making this a case of getting a upcoming figurehead in place as the calendars swap. Departing CEO Fredrik Wester isn't going far, at least for now, as he'll "continue focusing on the firm's long-term development as a member of the board".

"My plan was never to be CEO for life," Wester said. "The goal was to build the foundation before passing the baton on for the next chapter in the tech giant’s journey. Since I returned as CEO, we’ve streamlined our strategy, rebuilt our pipeline and developed our commercial offering. Mattias has had a central role in laying this foundation, and now is the right time to hand over.".

"The Board wants to thank Fredrik for his visionary leadership and outstanding contributions over these years," stated chairman Håkan Sjunnesson. "As a result, Paradox is in a strong position at a time when much of the industry is facing major challenges." He added that Lilja is "more than ready to assume the role and lead Paradox towards upcoming gaming experiences that last for decades".

Lilja himself declared that Paradox have "a unique DNA that has made us one of the greats in deep and engaging strategy and management games" and will be "stepping up the pace". "We will make further investments in our core business, push the boundaries of our game design, work even more closely with our loyal players, develop more and better tools and services that benefit both modders and players, and continue to sharpen our ways of working and our organisation, with player value in focus," he said.

As Wester alluded to, he previously served as Paradox CEO from 2009 to 2018, with a brief stint as executive chairman of the board sandwiched between that and his latest stint as CEO since 2021. Lilja has been deputy CEO since 2024 and chief of staff since 2021, having originally joined Paradox as a producer in 2009.

It has been revealed that the past half decade has been a very mixed bag for Paradox. Their major strategy flagships keep ticking along, albeit with the question of whether their next DLC will feel worth it hovering overhead near-permanently. Outside of that, however, the likes of Cities: Skylines 2, Vampire: The Masquerade Bloodlines 2, and cancelled Sims competitor Life By You have made for a track record heavy on questionable decisions and games which either flopped hard or failed to blow away expectations. Wester acknowledged back in 2024 that the tech giant had "made the wrong calls in several projects, especially outside of our core".

With the likes of post-apocalyptic strategy game Afterworld currently in the works, it'll be interesting to see if Lilja's tenure can see Paradox finally start to nail not just their nerdy bread and butter, but also games that don't involve staring down at a big map.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With less than a week to go before GTA 6's hugely anticipated release, the game's final map - or at least a stylised poster version of it, depicting the state of Leonida's key landmarks - has surfaced online. It was reportedly snapped during Selfridge's sizable GTA 6's takeover, and is seemingly the physical map included in Rockstar's £350 collector's edition.

Sources indicate that fans have been pondering GTA 6's map for some time now, cross-referencing previous map leaks with official trailer footage in an attempt to gain some insight into the major landmarks and regions Rockstar has in store. And while the newly leaked map is far from granular, it does at least appear to confirm Leonida's rough layout and the key locations players can visit this time.

Assuming the map's veracity, it's all rendered in an art style somewhere between mid-century tourism poster and Adult Swim, featuring the phrase "The Goodtime State" up top - a riff on the actual Florida's nickname, The Sunshine State - while Leonida's most notable points of interest are interspersed with cartoon figures.

There's a toking turtle (or possibly a tortoise - I'm no expert), a golfer proudly wearing assless chaps, a flying saucer, and more. I'll spare you the geographic details confirmed on the map in case you want to go in unspoiled. One point of amusement though: the way the map photo is cropped means fans searching for confirmation of an in-game Key West are still none the wiser.

According to recent reports, it's not entirely clear where the wonkily angled photo originated from, but prominent Rockstar Games community insider Videotech, who shared the image on social media, suggested it came from a "naughty Selfridges employee" during Selfridges' GTA 6 takeover. The map itself appears to be the "double-Sided souvenir poster with map of Leonida" included in Rockstar's eyewateringly expensive GTA 6 Collector's Edition. This costs £350 and doesn't come with a copy of the game. Or assless chaps, for that matter.

This isn't the first time GTA 6's map - officially noted to be twice the size of GTA 5's - has leaked online, although previous leaks have been notably more controversial. Earlier this year, a group calling itself CyberLeek shared unofficial gameplay and map details in the name of what it called "Gamers' Rights". In August, with Netflix's official GTA 6 unveiling looming, the group cashed out nearly £200,000 from its crypto scheme.

In a recent development, amid all this, Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion has been delayed until next week, meaning a verdict could arrive just as GTA 6 goes on sale.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, what's the best prank you ever pulled on a teacher in school, assuming you went to school? By which I mean, a genuinely funny prank that didn't cause any injuries, break any of the more important laws (legal or ethical), or leave anybody with years of mental distress.

According to recent reports, I'll start: I once had to write a four-page punishment essay with the topic "silence is golden", after being caught talking in class. I took the essay very seriously for the first three pages, only to end it with the phrase "...but not as golden as my arse." The teacher who set me the essay smugly tore it up without reading it - as I knew he would. Checkmate, Mr Thompson. Decades later, the last laugh remains mine.

It has been revealed that worst Class Ever is a fresh don't-call-it-friendslop asymmetrical multiplayer game dedicated to such larks. One player is a teacher, and seven others are naughty delinquent children, hiding in amongst some well-brought-up and obedient NPCs. As the wayward tykes, your goal is to do mischievous things like eating at your desk, passing notes, dropping banana skins, and playing on your phone, without being spotted by Teach.

All of this takes place in a breezy modern Japanese high school, the kind familiar from a million animes. Bagsy the Protagonist Desk by the window at the back of the class! The maplist spans the curriculum, from computer labs to gym tracks to stepped lecture theatres. I don't think there are any covert edu-tainment mechanics, but if you're playing Teacher, I guess there's nothing to stop you actually explaining the periodic table while trying to work out who keeps throwing chalk at your head.

What a wholesome and whimsical place! Such happy memories! Oh crikey, the male teacher is terrifying – why can't he stop grinning? And why do I have a smoke grenade? Why is this lesson taking place in the dark? Why are the teachers permitted to punch the students and tie them to wooden posts? Worst Class Ever definitely isn't a horror game, but I'm not sure I'd send my kids to this particular institution. I feel like we're one texture pack away from playing a more sociable version of Little Nightmares. Read more on Steam.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, knights of the Old Republic is my favorite RPG of all time, and a key reason why my love of video games developed as deeply as it did. My hopes for Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic, a spiritual successor to BioWare's classic, are sky-high, and expectations from the broader community are similarly intense. Director Casey Hudson isn't too worried about that pressure, though – after all, he and much of the team at Arcanaut Studios made the original KOTOR and the Mass Effect trilogy.

It has been revealed that "I think it would be really weird to do if I hadn't worked on the first one," Hudson admits in an interview for The Fourth Curtain podcast. "It would feel really strange. But I think, for us, we've got folks on the team who worked on that game and have worked on all the Mass Effect games since and other BioWare stuff.".

Hudson indicates that experience "helps," because the studio knows "why we did things the way we did. We're not trying to fill someone else's shoes, despite the expectations being really high.".

We still know very little about Fate of the Old Republic, other than the fact that it's a spiritual successor to KOTOR. What kind of gameplay systems will it build on? I can't imagine KOTOR's creaky D&D 3.5-based mechanics are going to make a comeback. What kind of story will it tell? It's going to have to be something all-new, with the entire Star Wars universe having been rebooted since KOTOR was new.

Sources indicate that "The thing that supersedes everything is our passion and excitement for doing something amazing," Hudson notes. "That has to outshine everything else, because you can't really know how to answer pressure, and it's hard to even really understand what other people want to play. But if you're so excited about making something that people are going to love, you're just passionate about it being amazing, that leads you to where you want to go.".

Sources indicate that that's maybe an obvious answer, but I appreciate that it's the one Hudson is providing. No new game can possibly live up to my nostalgic memories of BioWare's Star Wars RPG, and what I really want is a new game created by a team of people who are excited about what they're making. If it can tap into my old love for KOTOR, that's just icing on the cake.

Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic director Casey Hudson says there'll be "fresh announcements" about the KOTOR successor next year.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft has confirmed that it's laid off a total of 166 employees across two of its major studios, Ubisoft Montreal and Ubisoft Quebec.

Although this figure only accounts for roughly 4% of the publisher's full Canadian workforce, it's obviously still a lot of people to let go of in one fell swoop.

Based on an unnamed source, IGN reports that the layoffs are largely to do with Ubisoft's continued restructuring; it suggests that many of those impacted were working on projects that have since been cancelled.

Sources indicate that for context, Montreal has worked on almost every major Ubisoft game you can think of over the past couple of decades. It's right now developing Assassin's Creed Hexe, having spearheaded Assassin's Creed Valhalla and Assassin's Creed Origins previously.

Quebec, meanwhile, has been chiefly responsible for Assassin's Creed Syndicate, Odyssey, and the series' most recent instalment, Shadows.

"As our portfolio evolves, our production needs are changing, requiring us to adjust the size of some teams to ensure our resources are aligned with current production priorities and business needs," reads an official statement from Ubisoft.

"Those affected are being provided with severance, extended health care benefits, career transition services and other resources," it continues.

This console generation has proven tumultuous for Ubisoft as a whole, to the point where its production pipelines have been completely overhauled under Chinese tech giant Tencent's guidance. The company is still trying to streamline operations more than a year after all of that came into effect.

Naturally, we wish everyone impacted by these layoffs all the best for the future.

[source ign.com, via videogameschronicle.com, gematsu.com].

A newly introduced report reckons 40% of developers in the video games industry are using generative AI - but even more think it's harmful

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Despite all the outrage and criticism around game developers and publishers using generative AI in gaming, a upcoming report from the Game Developers Conference (GDC) calculates that as many as 40 percent of developers active in the industry use the controversial tools in their work.
  • That's according to the latest State of the Game Industry report from GDC, which gathers data from more than 2,300 respondents including, but not limited to, game industry professionals, made up of developers, producers, marketers, executives, and investors.
  • According to recent reports, the report notes that 57 percent of developers who say they do use it, use gen-AI for "text generation, research, early prototyping, coding, and presentations".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Despite all the outrage and criticism around game developers and publishers using generative AI in gaming, a upcoming report from the Game Developers Conference (GDC) calculates that as many as 40 percent of developers active in the industry use the controversial tools in their work. This is up four percent compared to the same report last year.

That's according to the latest State of the Game Industry report from GDC, which gathers data from more than 2,300 respondents including, but not limited to, game industry professionals, made up of developers, producers, marketers, executives, and investors.

According to recent reports, the report notes that 57 percent of developers who say they do use it, use gen-AI for "text generation, research, early prototyping, coding, and presentations". There appears to be a major split between triple-A studios that use gen-AI (with 27 percent of triple-A developers noting that they "feel encouraged or pressured" to use it) and indie devs, of which only nine percent say the same. Perhaps unsurprisingly - given how vocally against gen-AI a lot of 'frontline developers' have been - the tools are mostly used by "business operations and services, mobile-only studios, and free-to-play developers".

According to recent reports, there seems to be a gap in the ages of those willing to use AI tools as well; per the report, over half (54 percent) of people 45 years or older reported using the tools - an eight-point increase from last year's survey. There is also more usage among men (45 percent) than women (33 percent).

It has been revealed that what is perhaps more striking is that more people responded to the survey saying that they think AI is having a negative impact on games (55 percent) than responded saying they use the tech, suggesting a trend of caution rather than widespread adoption. Notably, respondents saying they are wary of the technology increased one percent since last year, so more people think AI is having a negative effect on the industry now than at the same time in 2025. Perhaps that's because of the sweeping layoffs we've seen across the games industry, often mentioned in the same breath as AI. Or the 'AI slop' that's been flooding Steam and pushing more traditional developers out. Orr some of the abysmal projects we've seen launch that have clearly used gen-AI assets.

"I did not get into a creative industry to hand over the creativity to an algorithm," mentioned one respondent from the UK when explaining why they don't use gen-AI tools. "I got into this industry to collaborate with creative people, not to have an advanced chatbot riff on the ideas of someone who was laid off," said another from California. "I believe that no one should have to read what no human has written and shouldn't have to see what no human has created," said yet another from Minnesota.

The use of generative AI remains controversial in the games industry, though with significant companies like Epic and Microsoft doubling down on the tech, it seems this split between developers that want to embrace it and those that don't is only growing larger.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, spoiler alert! This story discusses the ultimate winners of the reality competition series Win the Mall, now available with a Netflix subscription.

Somehow Netflix has become the place to go if you want to watch a reality TV competition set in an unexpected location. (Hey, Wonka’s The Golden Ticket, I’m looking at you.) I enjoyed and see more potential in Win the Mall in the future, the one thing that became immediately clear is that I would like to see more of the actual mall itself.

Recent findings suggest that it’s a simple idea. I mean, who hasn’t thought about at least spending the night in a mall, going on a shopping spree, and having free rein of the food court before sleeping in one of the mattress store’s beds? Clearly, it’s not just me, or there wouldn’t be this 2026 TV schedule release. I just wish we could have seen even more of the mall!

When you move 10 teams of two contestants into a shopping mall to compete for a $1 million grand prize, it feels like you should have a proposal to incorporate the mall as much as possible. Part shopping spree and part social strategy, players are dropped into a real mall, but the fake storefronts make it challenging to fully utilize the mall itself, leaving it all to feel a bit disconnected at times.

Industry observers note that the shopping spree challenges are the most fun because they see the teams ripping through the stores to guess what things cost to get close to their given dollar amount. It best embraces the chaos and energy of a shopping mall, especially on Black Friday. Something felt perfectly fitting about book-ending the season with shopping sprees, to introduce us to the competitors in the beginning and to narrow it down to the ultimate winner at the end. But that left six episodes in between where I wish I could have seen more of the actual mall.

Sources indicate that there are a lot of challenges that take place adjacent to the stores, but I wish they’d found a better way to incorporate them. There’s a Starbucks in play, but we never really see the inside of it. And there’s a KFC boasted about for its lounge, but they only briefly hang out there. I just feel like there could have been some inventive ways to incorporate some of the stores themselves instead of having so many challenges set in the center space.

Recent findings suggest that surprisingly, one of the highlights of Win the Mall is TikTok creator-turned-host Haley Baylee, who is truly delightful. She’s a likable host who can wear anything and look like she’s on a runway, but she also never takes herself too seriously, being goofy when she needs to be and taking on a more serious persona while tempting contestants with possible game advantages.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

It has been revealed that whether there’s ever another season of Win the Mall or not, I hope that we get to see more of her in the future. If we do get more, I just hope they can find a way to be more inventive in showing off more of the mall or even some “mall employees.” I liked a lot of the rest of the setup, and the contestants who ultimately won, but one possible idea is to incorporate some sort of sidekick for Haley Baylee who could be more directly related to the mall itself and could work as a bridge between the setting and the contestants. Just spitballing here.

There are a lot of great Netflix reality TV shows these days to choose from, including Squid Game: The Challenge, based on their own scripted programming. And while it wasn’t perfect, Win the Mall was entertaining and creative enough that I’d definitely watch another season. Don't let this one be a one and done, Netflix.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

World of Warcraft: Forever has a lot of changes from the classic version of the game, but one of the chief ones is that its items are different—and while I'm only just now starting to see actual, potential game-changing bits of kit (I've gotten into trinket-juggling between pulls), there have been some pretty flavourful pieces. Like Rockslicer, an axe that lets you mine ore.

In a recent episode of the official WoW: Forever podcast, senior game designer Aidan Moon spoke a little on his design philosophies, and items that players are yet to see: "There's a lot that they have not seen that I'm very happy with and I think is a great direction for the game.".

Industry observers note that moon's entire philosophy seems built around flavour over form, using the example of the Ogre Loincloth, a pair of cloth casting pants with strength, as a north star of sorts: "I just want to do something different that adds texture and crunch to the game. People will see things like the Ogre Loincloth, and they'll be like: 'Why does this cloth thing have strength on it?'.

"That's because, when we say we're a fantasy-forward game, that means that before optimisation, before it being good, it needs to be flavourful, it needs to feel like it belongs in the world and that the stats are essentially a storytelling mechanism for items.".

Ultimately, Moon thinks that interesting items that are memorable are far better for the game than a purely optimal numbers upgrade: "I would rather there be an Ogre Loincloth in the game that people talk about and get upset over, than just another strength belt that people go 'oh, that's just the mail strength belt in the dungeon'.".

As for what we're yet to get to, Moon, laughing, remarks: "I've done some stupid stuff.

According to recent reports, "There may be an item that is master looter BiS—I'll just put it that way … Maybe you get extra stats if your bags are completely full." Finally. An item for people who are allergic to inventory management! Me. I'm talking about myself. My bags are so full please send help.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The South Korean studio stated as much in its latest quarterly Earnings Letter, explaining that it had previously "validated game systems only after implementing them manually." 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crimson Desert and DokeV developer Pearl Abyss is planning to further integrate generative AI into its workflow.

The South Korean studio stated as much in its latest quarterly Earnings Letter, explaining that it had previously "validated game systems only after implementing them manually." Now, Pearl Abyss is using AI "to rapidly validate diverse design concepts prior to actual implementation," and argues the move "enables a more efficient allocation of development resources and enhances overall production speed.".

"However, AI serves strictly as a tool to support concept validation and pipeline productivity, while the core gameplay experience and actual content creation remain fully driven by our development team," the developer mentioned.

When Crimson Desert first launched, players spotted a crop of suspicious in-game images that looked like they were prompted into existence. Pearl Abyss soon explained that some "2D visual props" were generated with AI tools, but were always intended to be replaced with human-made art, before swiftly patching them out of the hit open-world game.

It has been revealed that it seems Pearl Abyss is now even more keen on the controversial tech, however: "We are integrating AI technologies to enhance development productivity and overall quality. AI is being utilized across various stages of development - including the automation of repetitive tasks, content creation support, and test optimization - and we are expanding its implementation throughout our entire development pipeline. We view AI not as a substitute for human developers, but as a tool to elevate development efficiency and quality. We will continue to expand our application of AI to deliver higher-fidelity games to the market more expeditiously.".

Industry observers note that elsewhere in the letter, the studio remarked its previously unveiled creature-collector DokeV is "targeting a launch in the second half of 2028" and we should hear more about it within the year. DokeV was initially targeting a 2023 launch a few years ago. Meanwhile, Crimson Desert is being prepped for a Nintendo Switch 2 launch "in the first half of next year.".

The use of generative AI in game development has been a hot topic for years, though it's only become more prevalent in recent months as 'AI slop' floods Steam and substantial companies like Epic Games proudly adopt the tech. A recent report even estimated that around 40 percent of active developers use AI tools in their work.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Legend of Zelda was in "dire straits" before Breath of the Wild gave the beloved series a massive second wind, according to two former Nintendo marketing leads.

Recent findings suggest that the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's most recent remake has been a mega success, becoming the fastest-selling Switch 2 game so far, but the shiny fresh adventure has also prompted some online debate over where the series should go next. Should Zelda lean into its carefully directed history - like the one brilliantly remade in Ocarina of Time - or keep the ball rolling with Breath of the Wild's wide open, spontaneous sandbox?

Nintendo of America's ex-director of social media marketing Kit Ellis and former public relations manager Krysta Yang chimed in on the discourse in their latest podcast (below), and explained that Zelda wasn't doing too hot before the Switch era.

"There has been some revisionist history out there lately," Ellis remarked in response to fans who reckon "the Zelda team ripped away" series staples, like classic dungeons and linear worlds, at the height of their popularity.

"I remember, I was going to the focus groups where it was a really dark moment," Ellis continued. "The feedback was like, 'The fan base is dwindling. This is not bringing in newly introduced players.'".

Industry observers note that the Legend of Zelda was supposedly "shrinking," while "interest in the audience was getting smaller and smaller" with each upcoming entry. "They had to do something dramatic," Ellis stated.

Industry observers note that "This series was in dire straits. They were selling, like, nothing," Yang added.

The Zelda series was certainly never irrelevant, but there's a pretty massive gap between the roughly 8m copies Twilight Princess sold at the beginning of the Wii generation, the roughly 3m copies Skyward Sword sold at the end of the console's life, and the 34m copies that Breath of the Wild sold just one console generation later.

In a recent development, it was a success so substantial it spawned a wildly ambitious sequel, Tears of the Kingdom, and even influenced the latest 2D Zelda, Echoes of Wisdom. Now that classic Zelda's back in the spotlight, though, I do hope Nintendo's able to slot the series' curated dungeons into whatever the next mainline game becomes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A mainstay of the GTA series has been the presence of sex workers, but Rockstar Games has dropped this aspect for the newly released GTA 6.

As reported by Shack News, unlike most other games in the long-running franchise, you cannot hire a sex worker in GTA 6.

The outlet asked Rockstar about this decision, and received the following response:.

Recent findings suggest that "GTAVI is a game about a couple in a bind, lovers on the run. While we have taken a lot forward from previous GTA titles, everything we have implemented in VI has been done to support the spirit of the story we wanted to tell, and the gameplay systems we wanted to expand upon - things like wanted system, the radio, robberies and car theft. Many aspects of previous titles are not present in GTAVI, but the elements we have we believe are all necessary and complementary to the feeling and motivations we wanted to emphasize as you play through Jason and Lucia's story.".

So, in other words, sex workers aren't included this time around because it wouldn't make sense for Jason or Lucia to pursue that, as they're already in a relationship — and that's a significant part of the story.

As mentioned, they have been present in the series since 2001's GTA 3, and this will be the first 3D game to exclude them.

GTA 6 is also the first game that centres on a couple, however, with the relationship between Jason and Lucia interwoven in the gameplay as well as being a key tenet of the narrative. It seems Rockstar didn't think sex workers would be conducive to this goal.

  • Latest Game Plus, as mentioned below, raises the level cap to 100, and scales enemies and regions in the game around you.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

UPDATE 17TH NOVEMBER: The Blood of Dawnwalker update 1.2 - the update that brings a New Game Plus mode, predominantly - is now available on PC, PS5, and Xbox Series S/X.

Latest Game Plus, as mentioned below, raises the level cap to 100, and scales enemies and regions in the game around you. Previously, the game was zone-scaled, so some zones were tougher than others. In New Game Plus, this will no longer be the case, so you can go and explore Xanthe's region at the back of Vale Sangora straight away, if you want to.

Recent findings suggest that there'll be new versions of equipment with new stats to find, and they'll be labelled with "NG+" so you know when you've picked one up. You can unlock New Game Plus from the main menu after choosing your base save and difficulty option. All of your accrued skill perks and abilities will be available to you at the start of the Withering Away quest in the game's prologue.

The full patch notes for Dawnwalker patch 1.2 are:.

ORIGINAL STORY 13TH NOVEMBER: A New Game Plus mode is coming to vampiric RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker next week.

Developer Rebel Wolves has now detailed everything coming with The Blood of Dawnwalker's Revision 1.2, right now planned to go live sometime next week, and top of the list of changes is a Newly introduced Game Plus for players who have already rolled credits on the game.

"If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with New Game+," the developer revealed earlier today. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over." Rebel Wolves is upping the level cap to 100 for New Game Plus, which will also have items with updated stats and enemies "balanced and scaled uniformly across all regions.".

Elsewhere in Enhancement 1.2, the studio is making tweaks to "enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat," and improving terrain geometry to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration." We'll need to wait for more comprehensive patch notes before finding out which enemies are getting spongier or flimsier, however.

While the incoming patch doesn't seem to be as beefy as the last - the one that added animal petting and an easier Story mode - it'll be a good way to sink your teeth deeper into a game that's already begging to be replayed, thanks to a time management mechanic that can drastically change any given run.

The fresh game from some former The Witcher 3 veterans came out in September and seems to have been a hit. Eurogamer's The Blood of Dawnwalker review called the game a "familiar dark fantasy adventure, but one with bold and provocative ideas of its own, that's mostly, enormously successful.".

While soulslikes went bigger than big, Death's Door swung open the appeal of a tighter adventure

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that declaring a Best Way of Doing Things is a fool’s game, though in recent years my favourite entries in the Tricky Hitting genre – inclusive of soulslikes and their hybridised disciples – have been the massive, bulging ones.
  • It has been revealed that even in the latter stages, with a full kit of precisely four ranged spells, Death’s Door is a simple proposition.
  • According to recent reports, still, it’s clever with its limitations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that declaring a Best Way of Doing Things is a fool’s game, though in recent years my favourite entries in the Tricky Hitting genre – inclusive of soulslikes and their hybridised disciples – have been the massive, bulging ones. Elden Rings and Silksongs, with vast kingdoms and deep, rattling toolkits for surviving them. The reason it’s a fool’s game is because you can also have something like Death’s Door, a taut, compact, lighthearted little actioner that fills eight hours instead of 80 and yet never feels underwhelming or compromised for it.

It has been revealed that even in the latter stages, with a full kit of precisely four ranged spells, Death’s Door is a simple proposition. You are a crow. You hit things. Occasionally you shoot things. You collect the souls of a frog, a yeti, and a grandmother. Everything in-between directly relates to finding the errant monster/pensioner, or at a stretch, upgrading one of those four abilities.

According to recent reports, still, it’s clever with its limitations. Environments are small in number but vary wildly in tone and texture, and they tightly weave their paths into criss-crossing bundles that maximise travel – evoking the sense of a great, ranging adventure within relatively tiny spaces. The lack of a wiki’s worth of combat options also never becomes a problem, partly because it spreads out its spell unlocks, and partly because the smooth, flowing back-and-forths of its central swordplay are pleasurable enough to carry it anyway. Good bosses, too! They’re all characterful, memorable weirdoes who fight unlike anyone in their minion armies, and usually come with a hidden weakness to deduce and exploit.

Which is welcome, as these big lads and lasses do tend to launch difficulty spikes right up your feathered backside, and do so in a game that isn’t otherwise as fussed about trial-and-error pain endurance as some of its inspirations. They don’t, however, bring the mood down. At times, this tale of a pitch-black soul reaper working as an agent of Death (complete with an office of Death and embittered co-workers of Death) can get downright cosy, leading through you through warmly-lit jungles and breezy waterside ruins.

Recently replaying, I’d also forgotten how witty it can be. Little gaglets are sprinkled throughout, both visual and verbal, but the best jokes are saved for – funnily enough – the bosses, who’ll raise your pre-fight spirit with some amusingly terrible trash talk before becoming the punchline themselves. I audibly wheezed the first time a death animation immediately cut to the foe’s impromptu funeral, their beaked killer among the precious few guests. And even when the joke is recycled later, I couldn’t help tittering at the sight of my enemy – who seconds earlier, had been attempting to fatally sit on me – lying nobly in state.

I previously considered ending my Valor Mortis review by calling it a gateway into the more demanding side of action-RPGs; a shorter, simpler alternative to FromSoft’s overwhelming titans that might nonetheless serve to introduce curious newcomers to their shared quirks and qualities. The game equivalent of splashing your chest with water before jumping into a pool. In hindsight, Death’s Door was always a better fit for that description, though there’s enough else here you don’t need to be prepping for something tougher to appreciate its lean, keen adventuring.

Recent findings suggest that for the last decade, Ben and Erin Napier have been renovating homes in the small Southern town of Laurel, Mississippi, on HGTV’s wildly popular show Home Town. The series’ 10th season premiered in January on the 2026 TV schedule, and fans, including me, have been itching for any sort of patch on the famous reality couple. In particular, I’ve been waiting for an update on Season 11, and Erin finally spoke out.

Season 10 wrapped up in March, and Erin revealed in August that filming had just started back up on the upcoming episodes. While there isn’t any information on when to expect Home Town''s exact return, there is one big piece of news that will surely make people happy: Erin took to her social channels earlier this week to share the episodes are just about done, and she even posted photos from the wrap party:.

A post shared by Erin Napier (@erinapier).

Industry observers note that considering it’s been a trying year for the Napiers, it’s great to see them finally able to celebrate something. Last December, the hotel they were renovating for their series, Home Town: Inn This Together, caught on fire, close to Erin’s 40th birthday.

Fans were able to see the hard work the couple and their team have put into the hotel for the spinoff, which ended with the hotel fire (streaming now with an HBO Max subscription), but I love that they can look forward to the future of Home Town, which is certainly not slowing down any time soon thanks to the Napiers and their incredible team:.

It has been revealed that season 10 will be all buttoned up in a couple of weeks but last night we celebrated. You all must know that there’s no way one person can manage the design processes of 9 houses at the same time, and so I get to lean on this incredible team. Together we make a blueprint then everyone goes on whatever journey the house gives them, shopping and making every design choice with me. They are the many eyes and hands and feet that get to these houses across the finish line and I get to be an editor in chief of sorts, and it feels like magic every time.

Welp, I didn't see this confusion coming. I’m excited to see what kind of houses the Napiers are renovating in the new season, which is billed as Season 10, but is actually Season 11. The Season 10 finale aired in March, so these new batch of episodes, coming sometime in 2027, will certainly be Season 11.

It's a little confusing, and the Home Town stars know it. Erin clarified why she referred to the new episodes as Season 10, rather than Season 11, when asked by a fan, and her response makes a lot of sense:.

So, because of a programming discrepancy like 4 years ago, the numbers are off! y'all will know Season 10 as Season 11.

Sources indicate that it’s definitely confusing, but I'm glad it was addressed. There are plenty of indicates whose production numbers don’t line up with episode numbers, for whatever reason. For instance, a significant Jeopardy! inconsistency Ken Jennings revealed last year was that the production numbers currently being used don’t equal the total number of episodes produced, all because of mistakes from decades ago.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Regardless, I’m relieved to know production is just about wrapped, meaning we’ll be getting the Napiers back on our TVs soon. It's also worth noting, fresh seasons of Home Town typically premiere in December or January, and since the new season is still being worked on for the next couple of weeks, if the pattern sticks, we could be looking the same timeline for Season 10 (11). For now, the wait continues!

'GTA 6' Runs Best on This Console

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (699 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Grand Theft Auto 6 might just be the most anticipated game of all time.
  • Now, few of us will buy a game console specifically for GTA 6—unless you don't already have a current-generation PlayStation or Xbox.
  • Rockstar confirmed as much in a post on Tuesday, which was meant to spread the news about pre-loading the game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 might just be the most anticipated game of all time. It's been 13 years since Rockstar dropped GTA 5, and after years of rumors, leaks, and official announcements, the sixth mainstream installment in the series is nearly here. In fact, anyone who pre-ordered the game digitally can now pre-load it onto their console, if you want to ensure you're ready to play the second the game comes out.

Now, few of us will buy a game console specifically for GTA 6—unless you don't already have a current-generation PlayStation or Xbox. (The PC version of the game isn't expected until at least early 2027.) But, as it turns out, there's one specific console that can run GTA 6 better than the rest.

Rockstar confirmed as much in a post on Tuesday, which was meant to spread the news about pre-loading the game. But, interestingly, it spurred a discussion about the performance of the game itself, as well as which consoles are best to run it.

In a recent development, no matter which console you play GTA 6 on, Rockstar notes that the game will only target 30 fps (frames per second). That's decided slow for a mainstream game in 2026. GTA 5 also shipped at 30 fps in 2013, but newer consoles can run it at higher frame rates. In fact, most games that launch on the latest generation of consoles can run at 60 fps, if not higher. While it's certainly not a dealbreaker, it is interesting that Rockstar's latest game can't run at a faster frame rate even on the PS5 Pro or the Xbox Series X.

To that point, Rockstar called out the PS5 Pro specifically in its post, announcing, "The PlayStation 5 Pro offers breathtaking visuals, with improved clarity through PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) and ray-traced shadows only available on PlayStation 5 Pro.".

PSSR is Sony's AI upscaler, similar to options like DLSS from Nvidia, which uses AI to add extra graphical information to games in real time. That allows developers like Rockstar to run the game at a lower resolution to save on processing power, but still boost the visuals to reach a higher perceived resolution. As such, it's not as ideal as running the game at a higher resolution natively, but it can help improve the visuals without pushing the hardware beyond its limits. Meanwhile, ray-tracing offers realistic lighting effects and can also be graphically intense.

Sources indicate that while PlayStation and Xbox players alike will be stuck at 30 fps, it seems only PS5 Pro gamers will be able to play the game with ray-tracing effects and AI upscaling. It's surprising that Xbox Series X players don't have similar benefits, as the hardware is more powerful than Xbox Series S. Rockstar didn't specify why only the PS5 Pro gets these upgrades.

Recent findings suggest that in the post, Rockstar also unveiled that the PS5 version of GTA 6 takes advantage of other PlayStation-exclusive perks, like high-fidelity haptic feedback in the DualSense controller, spatial audio rendering using the PlayStation's Tempest 3D audio, as well as improved load times—though Rockstar didn't specify what those load times would be. These perks apply to all PS5 consoles, not just PS5 Pros. Rockstar goes so far as to say that GTA 6 plays best on PlayStation 5 consoles.

It has been revealed that that's not to say that Microsoft's consoles are totally left out of the perks. Rockstar says that GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on both Xbox Series X and S, as well as Xbox One. In addition, both PlayStation and Xbox gamers can play GTA 6 using Remote Play, so no one has to physically play on their console if they want to game on the go.

According to recent reports, again, there's no reason to go out and buy a specific console for GTA 6, so long as you have something that can run the game. After all, PS5 Pros are difficult to find, especially without wildly overpaying. But it's interesting that Rockstar has managed to give Sony's consoles the extra perks here, particularly since the organization hasn't explained why that is.

When she wakes up, however, her eyes glow a ghastly bright green... implying that she is now under Doom's control. Ruh-roh!

Avengers: Doomsday hits UK cinemas on December 16 and worldwide on December 18. For more, check out how to watch the Marvel movies in order.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Netflix's long-gestating Magic: The Gathering animated series is called Planeswalker, and it's coming in 2027.

The title was revealed at MagicCon Atlanta, and Netflix shared a first look at the show on Twitter/X on 13th November. "Every great story begins with a spark. Here's your first look at Planeswalker, a new animated series based on Magic: The Gathering. Coming to Netflix in 2027", the company wrote, and shared a teaser, which you can see below:.

According to a synopsis shared with IGN, the series follows Chandra Nalaar, "a volatile pyromancer hunted for her gifts, and haunted by her past". It continues: "Confronted by an insidious force, Chandra and some of the most legendary Planeswalkers must harness their extraordinary abilities, navigate treacherous alliances, and battle their own inner demons to prevent a cataclysmic war that threatens to consume their very existence".

Sources indicate that netflix first announced a Magic: The Gathering series in June 2019, with Avengers: Endgame directors Joe and Anthony Russo attached, and it was originally due in late 2022. Two years in, the original showrunners departed over creative differences, and in September 2024, Netflix confirmed it had started again from scratch with Star Trek: Picard and 12 Monkeys showrunner Terry Matalas in charge.

IGN reports that Matalas, who most recently ran Marvel's VisionQuest, is running the show alongside Cindy Appel. Budapest-based studio DIGIC Pictures is handling the animation.

At the end of last month, we learned PUBG is also being turned into a live-action series for Netflix, with Donald Glover set to direct, write, executive produce, and star.

Industry observers note that glover is a two-time Emmy and Golden Globe winner, best known for Atlanta and Community. Krafton calls PUBG "one of the world’s most enduring gaming franchises", and notes the game, which is credited with popularising the battle royale genre, holds seven Guinness World Records.

  • In a recent development, coming up in mid-December, there's the Junker starting scenario, which I assume is all about trading scrap, rather than being a Prussian nobleman.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mucky and disreputable kiosk game Probably Stolen – Cyberpunk Shopkeeper Sim is getting three substantial updates over the next few months that add extra starting scenarios, building on the existing wealth of goods, materials, vocations and techs. Those starting scenarios range from peddling human meat to running the finest cyber-frappucino stall this side of Tannhäuser Gate. There are no hard release dates, and the contents of each upgrade may alter, but developers Questing Goose Studio have shared some rough timeframes.

In a recent development, coming up in mid-December, there's the Junker starting scenario, which I assume is all about trading scrap, rather than being a Prussian nobleman. You'll get a bespoke perk, new items, and the ability to hire, equip and send scavs on expeditions. This update will also include some minor expansions for the Fence and Gunsmith vocations – the latter will be able to flog or otherwise make use of shotgun shells, 25mm grenade rounds and a tier 3 handmade SMG, alongside new armour.

In a recent development, late January is when you'll "very likely" get the chance to be an Organ Dealer, care of the second major upgrade. "Players will start by buying different organs and fulfilling specific requests, and will later be able to grow or print organs," a Steam blog explains. You'll also be able to filter blood and remove diseases, with different blood types having different value modifiers. How will you get your hands on organs? By sending horrible black market thugs on foraging "expeditions".

Last but not least, the planned April enhancement will add the Street Food Vendor starting scenario. This lets you weave a livelihood around choice beverages and edibles from a range of cultures, supported by updates to the game's Aquaculture and Hydroponics tech. Sounds a lot cheerier than the organ trading racket, but then again, Probably Stolen will doubtless find a way to make it utterly grim. Guests at Sweeney's Cantina know better than to ask what our frappucinos are made of.

Are you playing Probably Stolen? It's been doing better than expected. I was keen on the demo, but my attention was lured away by a truly upsetting game about dogpeople in caves.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"I essentially wanna get rid of [best in slot gear (BiS)]. I think that BiS is not a good thing for a videogame that's supposed to be about roleplaying aspects of it—that's why I've introduced the creature subtype system (where things are more effective against [for example] murlocs), I've introduced a biome system.".

Recent findings suggest that "In the raid, it's different … In the raid, if you go to the left wing, that's snowy, if you go to the right wing, that's haunted, if you go down below, that's cavernous. Different parts of the raid will have different biomes. I think your BiS should be different every single boss if you're actually making a theoretical BiS list," via the official WoW Forever podcast.

I might be going against the grain here, but I'm honestly all for this—my one major hangup, the inventory management, is also swiftly addressed in the podcast, with principal game designer Kris Zierhut commenting that "we've thought about that a lot—it's not something we need right now, but we're going to give you bigger bags and better ways of organising and searching to find those things.".

That's my worries solved, then! Moon also chimes in and notes that "Back in Season of Discovery, I think the biggest bags we could give you were 32 slots … now you can make 98-slot bags. I open the bag and my screen just [explodes].".

Recent findings suggest that the major hullabaloo from player communities seems to be this idea that we're just doing resistance gear again. Back in Vanilla WoW, you'd have to farm a bunch of specific elemental resistance gear for specific raids, and it's something that nobody quite like that much.

According to recent reports, the way I see this being different, however, is that Moon is very specifically talking about a "theoretical BiS list". In other words, this biome and creature-matching only has to be completely aligned if you want to be maximally sweaty and pump the highest numbers you possibly can.

In a recent development, it does not seem like this gear is mandatory, and I think the actual motivation behind it seems better. Trading off a ton of damage just to get crappy gear pieces so you can survive feels bad, but realising you have the perfect-shaped peg to put into a hole (stop giggling) actually sounds satisfying.

Recent findings suggest that not that there won't be problems, but I would genuinely rather WoW: Forever try and experiment properly with its gear systems, instead of following the same formula that the main game's been trundling out for the past 20+ years. I am, bare minimum, willing to wait and see how it pans out.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Call of Duty Endowment is marking Remembrance Day and its 17th anniversary by encouraging Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone players to pick up its Valor Pack, with all of Activision's net proceeds going towards helping veterans find jobs.

The Call of Duty Endowment Valor Pack - which has been available since Modern Warfare 4 rolled out on 23rd October - was designed by the Endowment and Infinity Ward with US Marine Corps veteran and Medal of Honor recipient Kyle Carpenter in mind.

The items include a melee weapon blueprint inscribed with "Worth Fighting For", plus items called Relentless and Still Standing.

According to the Call of Duty blog, 100 percent of Activision's net proceeds from the pack (after VAT and sales tax) go to the Endowment.

To mark Remembrance Day, players who owned it and introduced either game before 6pm GMT on 12th November also received double XP tokens and a DMZ survival kit.

"Veterans bring incredible skills into the workplace after military service," stated Carpenter.

The Endowment, which supports veterans in the UK as well as the US, states it has now helped place more than 180,000 into "high-quality jobs", and wants to reach 200,000 by 2030.

Other partners are also raising money, with Pilot's round-up campaign raising more than £4.7 million ($6 million) for the Endowment since 2019. Polaris will also donate around £19,500 ($25,000) if players collectively complete 5 million rides in its DAGOR vehicle across Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone by 25th November.

It has been revealed that it comes two weeks after Activision apologised to bereaved families of the Itaewon crowd crush victims and confirmed it would remove real footage of the tragedy from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. Players discovered that the game's opening cinematic uses short news clips to depict fictional civilian casualties during a North Korean invasion of South Korea. Those clips have since been found to include archive footage from the 2022 Itaewon disaster, in which around 160 people died.

Call of Duty's anti-cheat team Ricochet recently unveiled it's officially cracking down on Warzone Agent.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that welcome to Holiday Office Hours From the Labs, a collaborative multimedia project in which Lifehacker, CNET, ZDNET, and Mashable harness the power of our product testing laboratory and our editors' expertise to offer the best gift-buying recommendations possible. In this episode, we're talking televisions.

According to recent reports, I recently did a deep dive into TV development history, checked out what was on shelves for 2026, and I concluded that the best gift TV you can give this year is, actually, a pair of sunglasses. The XBX by XReal video display glasses are basically a TV you can shove in your pocket. Check them out:.

It has been revealed that I looked past traditional sets for a couple of reasons. First, because as much as we all love a great show or movie, who actually buys someone a TV set as a gift? More importantly, there's the nature of television itself. Since it was invented in the late 1920s, television quality has been measured by how big the screen is and how clear and bright the picture is, but in 2026, a nothing-special 4K television delivers an image that is pixel-invisible to a typical viewer, and most of us don't have living rooms big enough to need a display bigger than 65 inches. I think the innovation in the space is going to come from the form factor and the use case, and what better form factor is there than a pair of sunglasses?

These glasses deliver the equivalent of a 142" TV viewed from across the room. It's hard to compare resolution to traditional TVs—technically, the display is 1080p in each eye, but because the TV is just millimeters from your eye, it looks much clearer than that. The peak brightness is 1,600 nits, bright enough for most rooms, and there's a totally opaque shield if you need it. The refresh rate is a crisp 120Hz. They support HDR10 and real-time SDR-to-HDR upscaling, offer billions of colors, and it's all in a package that weighs only 62 grams.

Then there are the use cases. It can act as a separate monitor for your computer; you can watch a different show than your roommate without bothering them; but most of all, these are great for flights. There is no situation in life that calls for a substantial screen TV more than a cross-country airplane flight. Slip these on with a pair of headphones, and you can fly to Boise in your own private, virtual theater.

They plug right into any device that supports USB-C video, there's no battery to remember to charge, and they cost less than $300. In other words: They're the perfect TV gift for the holidays, even if they aren't technically a TV.

Xbox is handing out bans to GTA 6 players for uploading game captures that 'accidentally' breach its family and online safety guidelines.

On by default, game captures automatically uploaded to Xbox Live servers are scanned for offensive imagery, including hate speech, drugs misuse, excessive violence, as well as nudity and sexual content.

Sources indicate that according to some Reddit sleuthing, GTA 6 players are being banned for uploading content captured on the beach in Leonida amongst other activities. The original poster claimed to have captured "zero nudity-just standard Vice City beach/coastal gameplay with NPCs in swimsuits/bikinis" before getting slapped with a ToS violation.

If you think about it, it would be odd to walk around a beach with a video camera filming the locals, but it's a bit silly to see Xbox players getting 2-day bans. The rulings appear to be automated and unappealable too.

Recent findings suggest that it's not clear if sexual content or nudity is the cause for the violation, but it's worth noting GTA 6 does contain full-frontal nudity. We'd recommend not spamming the capture button during those sequences. Xbox doesn't like that sort of thirsty behaviour.

Sources indicate that if you're worried about getting a 2-day ban in the height of GTA 6 fever, then perhaps you could consider turning off automatic uploads in your Xbox settings. Here's a quick guide on how to do this:.

Ubisoft is reportedly working on a newly introduced Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series.

Recent findings suggest that according to Insider Gaming, the project is in early development at Ubisoft Montreal under the codename Spades. It’s one of three upcoming projects reportedly in production at the studio, and sources suggest a second of those is also set in the Rainbow Six universe. Eurogamer hasn’t been able to verify the report.

Industry observers note that it’s not yet clear what form the new game will take, but Insider Gaming’s sources said it's "likely Vegas 3 rather than a remake" of an existing game. Insider Gaming expects it will be several years before Ubisoft officially announces a new Vegas game.

According to recent reports, rainbow Six Vegas rolled out in 2006, followed by Rainbow Six Vegas 2 in 2008. Since then, the series has centred on 2015's Rainbow Six Siege, and in August, Ubisoft announced Rainbow Six Tactics, a single-player, turn-based spin-off from Ubisoft Paris due in 2027.

Rainbow Six now sits under Vantage Studios, the Ubisoft subsidiary set up last year that also oversees Assassin’s Creed and Far Cry, and in which Tencent holds a 26.32 percent stake.

Last week, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on two new Assassin's Creed games: one set in ancient Rome, and a mobile spin-off set in Jerusalem. The leak came less than a week after Ubisoft issued a statement about the future of the Assassin's Creed series, insisting there are currently no new remakes of the series' past games in the works.

It's an honor to be the answer to a question on Jeopardy!, and I'd assume it's an even higher honor to be the answer for Final Jeopardy! So, with that in mind, it's always fun to see how people react to being the subject of a question featured on the show. Case in point: Ice-T had a very funny take when he found out that someone didn't know he was the answer to Final Jeopardy!.

Final Jeopardy! can literally make or break someone’s future on the long-running game show. The clues can range from history to literature to, yes, even pop culture. On the episode from the 2026 TV schedule that aired on October 28, Ice-T was the answer for the final round. Two people got it right, but one person was wrong. Ice-T addressed the moment while appearing on the Today Show and revealed just what he thinks of the whole ordeal:.

Sources indicate that I’m in a lot of crossword puzzles, because Ice-T, I-C-E-T, is a weird spelled thing. But Jeopardy, I’ve been in Jeopardy before, but Final Jeopardy. …. [They asked] who put out an album, Home Invasion, and also is the longest-running character in television. And the guy remarked Tim Allen. I think he was thinking about Home Improvement, right? But the two women got it right, and I only care about the women [laughs]. So, you know, he lost, and they won. But that’s how it goes. But Final Jeopardy!’s a significant deal.

Of course, being a clue on Jeopardy! is a significant deal, even if it does sting when someone does not know the answer. And as Ice-T pointed out, he’s been in plenty of clues over the years. That being remarked, it’s a lot different when you’re in Final Jeopardy!

Overall, I love that Ice-T wasn’t too hurt over being mistaken for Tim Allen, and instead focused on the fact that the two women got it right, which is all he cares about. I'm also very entertained by the image of Tim Allen trying to rap.

Anyway, the clue was for the category “Current TV Streaks,” and it just shows that even if a clue seems easy, it may not be for a lot of people. For host Ken Jennings, there was one category that made him nervous when he was competing, and it was surprisingly hockey. While he wound up being one of the biggest Jeopardy! winners of all time and no one has yet to beat his 74-game streak, it sounds like that still haunts him. So, everyone has their blind spots.

Industry observers note that meanwhile, that Final Jeopardy! clue made me realize something truly insane. Despite the fact that Law & Order: SVU is in its 28th season, it’s wild to me that Ice-T has been playing Odafin “Fin” Tutuola for almost three decades. He’s been on the NBC drama since the second season and is one of the longest-running actors in the Law & Order franchise. Luckily, he doesn’t have any looks to leave any time soon. While he has been worried that he’d be written out as the show has had to make room for Kellie Giddish, that has not been the case.

It has been revealed that hopefully, the next time Ice-T is an answer for Final Jeopardy! everyone gets it right. However, even if it’s just the women, I’m sure he will be just fine. In the meantime, fans can catch him on Law & Order: SVU on Thursday, December 3, at 9 p.m. ET on NBC, streaming the next day with a Peacock subscription.

According to recent reports, A substantial part of the point of The Blood of Dawnwalker is that you're on a fixed time limit. You've got 30 in-game days and nights to try and save your family, and if you don't manage to see everything the game has to offer, well, the game's director is fine with that. But that doesn't matter as much now, as The Blood of Dawnwalker is getting its 1.2 revision next week that adds in a new game plus mode.

"If you completed the Epilogue, you can dive right back into Vale Sangora with New Game+!" a post from the devs explains. "Your level, skills, and inventory will carry over; the level cap will be raised to 100; enemies will be balanced and scale uniformly across all regions; and items will have NG+ versions with updated stats." Sounds like your usual new game plus affair! I suppose it is a good opportunity to try out different things compared to your first playthrough, but I'm not exactly aligned with the idea that the timer restriction is too restricting (as some mods have made clear how others feel that way).

In any case, the enhancement goes a tad further than that. If you got the Eclipse Edition of the game, the in-game soundtrack that came with it "will be extended with additional songs from the game." You can expect the soundtrack on streaming services soon, too. While details are slimmer here, there are also some planned balance changes, like updated enemy health pools and how often they use their abilities during combat, and terrain geometry has seen some improvements to allow for "smoother movement during combat and exploration.".

It has been revealed that overall, a bit of a smaller patch compared to the last one, but one I'm sure will be welcome to some all the same. If you've not had a chance to check the game out yet and still feel on the fence about it, here's some lovely words from Mark's review: "There’s always that sense that something important or unexpected could be lurking around the next corner, to pull you into a quest dripping with depth and intrigue. It works to ensure the more busywork-esque tasks attached to angering Brencis and his Boyars never make Vale Sangora feel home to a string of boring boxes to tick. It’s a vibrant, constantly changing place with a thousand different threads metaphorically criss-crossing just beneath its surface, just as ancient ruins literally criss-cross beneath its swamps, crags, and forests.".

We are now just four days away from the release of GTA 6 on Xbox Series X/S and PS5, but the proximity to the much-anticipated launch date isn't stemming the tide of leaks that has been plaguing the game for much of the past year. Yesterday, a latest video - seemingly from a record store that received vinyl records of the soundtrack early - revealed off the full 34-song tracklist for the game.

According to recent reports, thanks to the listing printed on the back of Grand Theft Auto 6: The Album vinyl, we have a better idea of the licensed music that'll appear in-game. Travis Scott, Rina Sawayama, Cardi B, Pinkpantheress, SZA, Keith Richards, Dua Lipa, Jennie, Lana Del Rey, Zara Larsson are just some of the names that make up the impressive list. We know about a few of these tracks from September's announcement of the record, but only six tracks were revealed then, not the whole list.

Take a look at the full track listing below:.

You can expect to hear these tracks on the radio - alongside many more, no doubt - and deployed at curated times during cutscenes or in missions, to really tie together the vibe of the city. This is something Vice City did remarkably well its roster of 80s tracks, and I can't wait to see how Rockstar has used more contemporary music in the same way here.

In a recent development, of course, there have been a lot of Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks in the run-up to the game's launch. Another recent example is the full game's map which seemingly leaked online thanks to the £350 collector's edition on show in a UK department store. Then there were all the leaks from a group calling itself CyberLeek, which shared unofficial gameplay and map details over the course of a few weeks, before Rockstar had even revealed much gameplay itself.

Sources indicate that amongst all this, Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week, as the game goes on sale.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ahead of the launch of GTA 6, there was a whole lot of talk online about the Xbox "New Zealand trick" and how people could get early access to the game by switching their regions to New Zealand on Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S.

We mentioned in various articles how it was a risky practice (against Xbox's ToCs), but one that had never traditionally resulted in any widespread bans, and it doesn't seem like either Xbox or Rockstar took any action at first glance.

As it turns out, a lot of people decided to give it a go for the newly introduced Grand Theft Auto.

This is according to the folks at Ampere Analysis (via The Game Business), who report that over 2.1 million people played GTA 6 in the US and the UK before it was officially released.

In a recent development, as you can see from the graph above, it seems the vast majority of those were based in the United States, followed by the UK, Canada, Brazil and Mexico. Only around 100,000 people tried the trick on PS5 in the U.S. (where it's harder to implement and requires a separate account), whereas 1.5 million of them ended up using it on Xbox.

In a recent development, ultimately, the existence of the Fresh Zealand trick probably led to a bunch of increased sales for Xbox Series X and Xbox Series S, but it also poses the question of whether Xbox might be forced to put a stop to it on Project Helix and beyond. As much it's a beloved feature, it's also being used in a way that wasn't originally intended.

Let's see what happens in the future, but for now, it's clearly made a lot of people happy this week!

According to recent reports, did you use the Latest Zealand trick for GTA 6? Let us know your experiences with it in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you're playing GTA 6 on Xbox, you should turn off your console's automatic upload feature or you could risk having your Xbox account suspended. An Xbox user on Reddit reported receiving a two-day, unrepealable ban for automatically uploading a 28-second clip of GTA 6 characters at the beach. According to the Reddit user, sangobar, the clip was almost immediately flagged by the Xbox Network for either violating the Xbox Community Standards or Microsoft Services Agreement terms (the email they received from Xbox doesn't specify which). However, the user claims the clip only showed characters in beachwear and the clip was therefore incorrectly flagged.So, to avoid the risk of an Xbox ban it is better to be safe than sorry, to disable your Xbox automatic upload feature, and to understand what Xbox's guidelines are around the content you can upload to the Xbox Network.

Sources indicate that automatic uploads to the Xbox Network are enabled as standard on Xbox, meaning the GTA 6 clips you capture on your console are automatically uploaded to the Xbox Network. To turn off your Xbox Series X's automatic uploads feature, follow these steps:.

One Drive is more lenient in what you can upload, but if you'd rather not automatically upload any of your GTA 6 capture, it's best to set both it and Xbox Network to 'Don't Upload'.

GTA 6 clips could potentially violate the 'Keep your content clean' term of the Xbox Community Standards, specifically the 'Make stuff that's suitable for all audiences rule', which states: "The Xbox community must be friendly and accessible to everyone, this isn't the appropriate place for sexual content. Keep your public posts and messages suitable for all ages and audiences.".

According to Xbox, some examples of content that could violate this term include sharing or distributing non-consensual intimate imagery, links or imagery that displays pornography, screenshots or game clips that include mature sexual content, custom gamerpics that contains nudity, lewd messages to other players, and distasteful or inappropriate pictures. In other words, be careful before sharing images or clips of GTA 6's more mature content, like GTA 6 strip clubs.

  • Recent findings suggest that in a new interview with IGN, the duo reveal that they had thought about adapting the Blade Runner fracnhise into a game, and that - should it come to fruition - it would target "triple-A" in scope.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blade Runner 2099 - an upcoming TV miniseries coming to Amazon Prime Video, acting as a sequel to Blade Runner (1982) and Blade Runner 2049 (2017) - might be getting a video game. And a 'triple-A' video game, at that. At least that's according to Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson, executive producers for Blade Runner 2099 and co-CEOs of Alcon Entertainment (which owns the Blade Runner IP).

Recent findings suggest that in a new interview with IGN, the duo reveal that they had thought about adapting the Blade Runner fracnhise into a game, and that - should it come to fruition - it would target "triple-A" in scope. Other than that, the duo seemed to want to keep any potential information to themselves. Given they appear to be in talks about the title, rather than in any active development, if something did come of this ideation, it would no doubt be a long, long way off. Kosove and Johnson's aim seems to be getting players to "interact" more with the world of Blade Runner, which has recently been fleshed out by the 2017 movie and is set to be developed more in the upcoming series.

Recent findings suggest that of course, we've seen Blade Runner games before. There was 1997's simply-titled Blade Runner - developed by Westwood Studios and published by Virgin Interactive - which was a point-and-click adventure that really seemed to pick up the vibes the original Ridley Scott was putting down. An Enhanced Edition of the game was released in 2022, which is actually more of a remake than a simple enhancement.

It has been revealed that then, in 2023, Annapurna Interactive unveiled its very first internally-developed game, in the form of Blade Runner 2033: Labyrinth. The game, which promised to riff on the dystopian universe established in Ridley Scott's cult classic movie, would have been sandwiched squarely between that film and its sequel, Blade Runner 2049. It was going to be set in LA after the Blackout hits, but beyond that - and the fact it's coming to PC and consoles at some point - few details ever managed to break through the PR barrier before the game went dark: it's been removed from Annapurna's website and delisted from Steam. Curious.

If you want to see something more from the cyberpunk world sooner, Blade Runner 2099 releases on Prime Video on 25th November.
